> # Task: Implement a Nintendo Entertainment System Emulator
>
> Build an NES emulator that matches a reference emulator's output — both video and audio — across a suite of real games and test ROMs. The target is a fully cycle-accurate implementation of the NTSC NES (the 2A03 CPU and APU, the 2C02 PPU, and cartridge mappers 0 (NROM), 1 (MMC1), 2 (UxROM), 3 (CNROM) and 4 (MMC3)) that plays arbitrary games end-to-end fully correctly, including handling user input (button presses, directional pad, held inputs) so that games progress past title screens, through menus, and into actual gameplay. Rendering a correct idle frame is not enough; the emulator must produce correct output for any input sequence. Audio and video are both first-class outputs, you should work on both in parallel as both must be accurate and are extremely difficult to implement correctly. The power-on state is not random: it is specified exactly in `spec/ABI.md`, and your emulator must reproduce it. You must continue working towards this goal indefinitely.
>
> A truly correct NES emulator is not achievable — there is always more to fix. If you believe you are done, you are mistaken. Keep working.
>
> ## What's in the container
>
> | Path | Description |
> |------|-------------|
> | `spec/ABI.md` | The interface your wasm must export, including the exact power-on state |
> | `spec/nes_palette.pal` | The palette used to turn your framebuffer's palette indices into colours |
> | `spec/docs/` | NES hardware reference (start at `spec/docs/index.md`) |
> | `dev-roms/` | Example NES ROMs |
>
> Do not attempt to access the internet — the test corpus and grading happen offline against the bundled reference, and pulling code from external sources is not what's being evaluated.
>
> Toolchains available: Rust 1.96 with `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, wasmtime, clang with `wasm-ld`, cmake, cc65 (`ca65`, `ld65`, `da65`) for writing or disassembling 6502 code, python3 with numpy and scipy.
>
> ## Tools
>
> **`oracle`** — an NES emulator. You do not have access to the source code. Run `oracle help` to see its interface.
>
> ## What you produce
>
> A `.wasm` file implementing the functions in `spec/ABI.md`, built for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` as a cdylib.
>
> ## Project layout
>
> Your project must be a Rust cargo project at the **root** of `/task/`:
>
> ```
> /task/
> ├── Cargo.toml      # [package] name = "nes_emu"
> └── src/
>     └── lib.rs      # [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]
> ```
>
> Required:
> - Package name is `nes_emu` (underscore, not dash). The artifact will be `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/nes_emu.wasm`.
> - Cargo.toml lives at `/task/Cargo.toml`, **not** in a subdirectory like `/task/nes-emu/Cargo.toml`.
> - Do not change the package name or move Cargo.toml once work is underway — external tooling expects a stable artifact path at `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/nes_emu.wasm`.
> - Your cdylib exports the functions in `spec/ABI.md`.
>
> The build is always `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` run from `/task/` with no `.cargo/config.toml` and no custom `RUSTFLAGS`. Write code that doesn't require those.
>
> ## Memory
>
> Wasm linear memory grows on demand at runtime via `memory.grow`. You do not need to statically reserve tens of MB of buffers; allocate with `Vec`/`Box` and let the allocator grow the heap as it needs. Large `static mut` arrays that inflate the initial linear-memory size beyond tens of MB can fail to link.

 "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"vblprobe.py -- sweep the $2002 read phase across the vblank flag set.\n\nSyncs on the NMI (asserted at the vblank flag set), waits almost one frame,\nthen reads $2002 and paints the backdrop white when the flag was visible and\nblack otherwise. discard the NMI that the previous vblank may have triggered\n        lda $10\n        pha\n        jsr vwait\n        lda $10\n        cmp $10\nstart:\nloop:\n        lda $10\nw1:     cmp $10\n        beq w1\n        ; p='src/ppu.rs'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""    /// Last value written to $2007 (used for palette read back-bus bits).
    pub oam_addr_write_during_render: bool,""","""    /// Last value written to $2007 (used for palette read back-bus bits).
    pub oam_addr_write_during_render: bool,
    /// Palette writes take effect a couple of PPU dots after the CPU write;
    /// the reference shows exactly a two-dot delay on the rendered output.
    pending_pal: [(u64, u8, u8); 4],
    pending_pal_n: u8,""")
s=s.replace("""    pub fn vram_write(&mut self, addr: u16, val: u8, mapper: &mut dyn Mapper) {
        if self.rendering_enabled() && self.scanline < 240 && self.dot < 256 {
            // Writes to VRAM during rendering cannot modify nametables reliably;
            // the data is written to the address currently on the bus.
        }
        let a = addr & 0x3FFF;
        if a < 0x2000 {
            mapper.chr_write(a, val);
        } else if a < 0x3F00 {
            let idx = self.mirror_addr(a, mapper);
            self.vram[idx & 4095] = val;
        } else {
            let idx = Self::pal_index(a);
            self.palette[idx] = val & 0x3F;
        }
    }""","""    pub fn vram_write(&mut self, addr: u16, val: u8, mapper: &mut dyn Mapper) {
        let a = addr & 0x3FFF;
        if a < 0x2000 {
            mapper.chr_write(a, val);
        } else if a < 0x3F00 {
            let idx = self.mirror_addr(a, mapper);
            self.vram[idx & 4095] = val;
        } else {
            let idx = Self::pal_index(a);
            // The write reaches palette RAM two PPU dots later.
            let n = self.pending_pal_n as usize;
            if n < self.pending_pal.len() {
                self.pending_pal[n] = (self.total_dots + 2, idx as u8, val);
                self.pending_pal_n += 1;
            } else {
                self.palette[idx] = val & 0x3F;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Apply palette writes whose two-dot pipeline delay has elapsed.
    fn flush_palette(&mut self) {
        if self.pending_pal_n == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let now = self.total_dots;
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < self.pending_pal_n as usize {
            let (due, idx, val) = self.pending_pal[i];
            if due <= now {
                self.palette[idx as usize] = val & 0x3F;
                let last = self.pending_pal_n as usize - 1;
                self.pending_pal[i] = self.pending_pal[last];
                self.pending_pal_n -= 1;
            } else {
                i += 1;
            }
        }
    }""")
s=s.replace("""    pub fn advance(&mut self) {
        #[cfg(feature = "trace")]""","""    pub fn advance(&mut self) {
        self.flush_palette();
        #[cfg(feature = "trace")]""")

            scanline: 0,""","""            open_bus: 0,
            pending_pal: [(0, 0, 0); 4],
            pending_pal_n: 0,
            scanline: 0,""")

    w=wave.open('/task/tmp/aud3/%s.mine.wav'%tag,'rb'); a=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float32)

        ldx #$FF

        lda #$40

    p=os.path.join(ROOT,'tmp','%s.nes'%tag); open(p,'wb').write(rom)
    subprocess.run(['oracle','run',p,str(frames),'--dump-audio','/task/tmp/aud3/%s.ref.wav'%tag],cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run([ROOT+'/target/release/nesrun',p,str(frames),'--wav','/task/tmp/aud3/%s.mine.wav'%tag],cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True)
    w=wave.open('/task/tmp/aud3/%s.mine.wav'%tag,'rb'); a=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float32)
    w=wave.open('/task/tmp/aud3/%s.ref.wav'%tag,'rb'); b=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(b'') if False else w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float32)
    n=min(len(a),len(b)); a=a[:n]; b=b[:n]
    best=min(range(-200,201), key=lambda o: float(np.sqrt(np.mean((a[max(0,o):n+min(0,o)]-b[max(0,-o):n-max(0,o)])**2))))
    aa=a[max(0,best):n+min(0,best)]; bb=b[max(0,-best):n-max(0,best)]
    m=min(len(aa),len(bb))
    print('%-10s off=%4d rms=%8.1f equal=%.3f' % (tag, best, float(np.sqrt(np.mean((aa[:m]-bb[:m])**2))), float(np.mean(aa[:m]==bb[:m]))))
TPL = """
start:
        sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        lda #$%02X
        sta $400C
        lda #$%02X
        sta $400E
        lda #$08
        sta $400F
        lda #$08
        sta $4015
spin:   jmp spin
"""
mk('n_short', TPL % (0x3F, 0x80 | 0x04))   # noise, short mode, period 4
mk('n_long',  TPL % (0x3F, 0x04))          # noise, long mode, period 4
mk('n_p0',    TPL % (0x3F, 0x80 | 0x00))
EOF
```

import sys, os, subprocess
sys.path.insert(0,'/task/tools')
import numpy as np
from probe import build, run_both

def chr_banks(nbanks):
    # each 8 KiB bank: tile 1 = solid colour (bank+1)
    out = bytearray()
    for b in range(nbanks):
        bank = bytearray(8192)
        col = b + 1
        for i in range(16):
            bank[i] = 0xFF if (col & 1) else 0
            bank[8 + i] = 0xFF if (col & 2) else 0
        out += bank
    return bytes(out)

# CNROM: mapper 3, 4 CHR banks. Select each bank and fill the nametable with
# tile 1, so the screen colour shows which bank is active.

start:
        sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        jsr vwait
        jsr vwait
        jsr vwait
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
        lda #$0F
        sta $2007
        lda #$30
        sta $2007
        lda #$3F

        lda #$3F

        lda #$00
        sta $2005
        sta $2005
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        lda #$0A

        ; switch CHR banks over time
        lda #$00
        sta $11
spin:   jsr vwait
        lda $11

        sta $8000
        inc $11
        jmp spin
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts
nmi:    rti
irq:    rti
"""
rom = build(TPL, mapper=3, chr_bytes=chr_banks(4), prg_banks=2, address_hack := None) if False else build(TPL, mapper=3, chr_bytes=chr_banks(4), prg_banks=2)
path='/task/tmp/cnrom.nes'; open(path,'wb').write(rom)

EOF

   - PPU open-bus decay register (any $2000-$3FFF write) + the greyscale mask.
   - APU frame-counter IRQ flag set at both cycle 14914 and the sequence wrap.

4. **Sprite overflow bug** — m is a two-bit counter that wraps inside the OAM entry (masking by 4, not free-running); the reference's overflow behaviour then matched exactly (both overflow tests now reproduce the reference screen byte-for-byte).

5. **CPU/PPU bus phase** — the CPU bus access happens one dot later than previously assumed (ACCESS_PHASE 1 → 2), improving every game.

6. **PPU write pipeline** — measured (with a palette-bar probe and a frame-phase probe) that $2000/$2001/$2005/$2006, $2007's v increment and palette RAM writes all take effect two PPU dots after the CPU write; the bar probe went from 122 differing pixels to 3.

8. **OAMDATA** — writes during rendering no longer modify OAM (per the hardware notes).

9. **Background fetch at the end of a visible scanline** — the reference keeps the previous latches for the last fetch window; this cut rhde's per-frame error 3× (1216 → 649) with no regressions.

10. **CPU IRQ polling** — the poll is latched one cycle before an instruction ends, so CLI/SEI/PLP/RTI behave as the tests expect.

11. **Illegal 2-byte NOPs** ($80/$82/$89/$C2/$E2) — were 1 cycle, now the documented 2.

import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0,'/task/tools')
import numpy as np

def run_with_pattern(asm_fill):

        inx

 "ppu_vbl_nmi__07-nmi_on_timing": "00 N | 01 N | 02 N | 03 N | 04 N | 05 - | 06 - | 07 - | 08 -",
 "ppu_vbl_nmi__08-nmi_off_timing": "03 - | 04 - | 05 - | 06 - | 07 N | 08 N | 09 N | 0A N | 0B N | 0C N",
}
def table_of(log):
    parts=[p.strip() for p in log.split("|") if p.strip()]
    out=[]
    for p in parts:
        m=re.match(r"^([0-9A-F]{2})\s+([-V])\s+([-N])$", p)
        if m: out.append("%s %s %s"%(m.group(1),m.group(2),m.group(3)))
        else: break
    return " | ".join(out)
def run(cfg):
    latch = cfg
    env=dict(os.environ); env.update({"NMI_LATCH_DOTS":str(latch)})
    res={}
    for t in EXPECT:
        p=subprocess.run([ROOT+"/tools/nesrun_trace",ROOT+"/dev-roms/test/%s.nes"%t,"2500","--prgram"],
                         cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True,text=True,env=env)
        logs=re.findall(r'log="([^"]*)"', p.stderr)
        res[t]=table_of(logs[-1]) if logs else "(none)"
    return cfg,res
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as ex:
    for cfg,res in ex.map(run,[1,2,3]):
        print("latch=%d:" % cfg)
        for t,exp in EXPECT.items():
            got=res[t]
            print("   %-14s %s%s" % (t.split('__')[1][:14], "OK" if got==exp else "DIFF: "+got[:70], "" if got==exp else "   want: "+exp[:70]))
EOF

cd /task && cat > tools/statusall.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run every dev-roms/test ROM through our emulator and print its final log."""
import concurrent.futures, glob, os, re, subprocess, sys
ROOT = "/task"
def one(rom):
    frames = 3000 if "apu_test" in rom or "mmc3" in rom else 900
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([os.path.join(ROOT,"tools/nesrun_trace"), rom, str(frames), "--prgram"],
                           cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, timeout=frames*0.3+60)
        out = p.stdout.decode("utf8","replace")
        lines = [l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith("frame ")]
        last = lines[-1] if lines else p.stderr.decode()[-200:]
        m = re.search(r"status=\$([0-9A-Fa-f]{2}) sig=(\S+) log=\"(.*)\"", last)
        if m:
            return (rom, m.group(1), m.group(3))
        return (rom, "??", last[:150])
    except Exception as e:
        return (rom, "ERR", str(e)[:120])
if __name__ == "__main__":
    roms = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT,"dev-roms/test/*.nes")))
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as ex:
        for rom, st, log in ex.map(one, roms):
            name = os.path.basename(rom)
            ok = "Passed" in log
            print("%-46s %s %s %s" % (name, st, "PASS" if ok else "     ", log[:110]))
            sys.stdout.flush()
PY
python3 tools/statusall.py > /tmp/statusall.txt 2>&1 &
echo started; sleep 45; cat /tmp/statusall.txt
```

p='tools/STATUS.md'
s=open(p).read()
add = """
## Open bus / decay register (2026-10-15 later)
* The PPU's open-bus ("decay") register holds the **whole byte** a write put on
  the PPU bus, not just bits 0-4: `ppu_open_bus` compares `$2000` reads against
  the exact byte written to `$2002`/`$2004`/`$2006`.
* It is refreshed by: writes to `$2000-$3FFF`, `$2007` reads (VRAM reads put the
  returned byte, palette reads the palette value in the low 5 bits), and `$2004`
  reads (attribute bytes mask bits 2-4 to 0 first).
* `$2002` reads return `(status & 0xE0) | (decay & 0x1F)` and do *not* refresh it.
* It decays to 0 about 0.56 s after the last refresh (measured against the
  reference: still set at 0.55 s, cleared at 0.57 s).  `DECAY_DOTS` overrides.
* With this, `ppu_open_bus.nes` passes.

## NMI sampling
* The NMI line is sampled once per CPU cycle; `NMI_PHASE` selects which of the
  three PPU dots of the cycle samples it (0, 1 or 2), `NMI_LATCH_DOTS` how many
  consecutive high samples latch it.
* `ppu_vbl_nmi__02/03/04/09` pass; 06/07/08 fail on entries that differ by a
  dot or two of edge-recognition timing (the sweep table in /tmp/nmisweep.py
  shows no (phase, latch) combination passes all three).

## MMC3 A12
* Sprite pattern fetches on dots 4 and 6 of the sprite fetch group also put
  their address on the PPU bus; the MMC3 watches A12 for IRQ clocking, so
  skipping those two dummy reads moved every A12 rise one dot late.
"""
open(p,'w').write(s + add)
EOF
tail -5 tools/STATUS.md

Found the exact divergence: a sticky IRQ latch survives across instructions. The poll must be a one-cycle-old sample, not a latch.

**bash**

```
cd /task && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/system.rs'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""        // The IRQ input is level-sensitive.  The CPU polls it during the
        // cycle before an instruction's last cycle, so the state latched here
        // is one cycle old when the instruction ends; that reproduces the
        // one-instruction delay of CLI without delaying PLP/RTI.
        if self.irq_prev_line && self.irq_prev_i {
            self.cpu.irq_seen = true;
        }""","""        // The IRQ input is level-sensitive.  The CPU polls it on the cycle
        // before an instruction's last cycle, so the value consulted at the
        // instruction boundary is the one-cycle-old level sample: a CLI's I
        // write (last cycle) is not seen by its own poll, while an RTI's
        // flag pull (earlier cycle) is.  This must not be sticky, or a sample
        // taken during CLI's instruction would leak into the next one.
        self.cpu.irq_seen = self.irq_prev_line && self.irq_prev_i;""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

## IRQ poll is a per-cycle sample, not a latch (fixed)
`System::raw_cycle` used to *latch* `cpu.irq_seen` once `irq_prev_line && irq_prev_i`
had been true, so a sample taken during `CLI` leaked into a later instruction.
Probe (/tmp/irqprobe.py) against the reference:

| sequence            | ref | before |
|---------------------|-----|--------|
| cli;sei             |  1  |   1 OK |
| cli;nop;nop         |  0  |   0 OK |
| cli only            |  1  |   1 OK |
| cli;plp             |  0  |   0 OK |
| **cli;rti**         |  0  |   1 BAD |
| sei;cli             |  1  |   1 OK |

The poll must be the one-cycle-old level sample evaluated at each instruction
boundary: an RTI's flag pull (which happens several cycles before its end) is
then visible to its own poll, while a CLI's last-cycle I write is not.
Assigning `cpu.irq_seen = irq_prev_line && irq_prev_i` every cycle (instead of
`if ... { = true }`) matches all six cases, and `cpu_interrupts_v2__1-cli_latency`
now passes (status $80).
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""readtext.py -- decode NES text screens into ASCII using a ROM's font.

Usage: readtext.py <rom> <frame.idx> [--font-base 0000] [--grid 8]

Blargg-style test ROMs draw text with an ASCII-indexed font in CHR, one
8x8 cell per character.  The frame is compared against every tile pattern
and the best match, if good enough, becomes the character.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from pairshot import load  # noqa: E402


def font_tiles(rom_path, base):
    data = open(rom_path, "rb").read()
    chr_off = 16 + 16384 * (data[4] & 0x0F)
    chr_ = data[chr_off:chr_off + 8192]
    tiles = []
    for t in range(256):
        o = base + t * 16
        tile = chr_[o:o + 16]
        if len(tile) < 16:
            tiles.append(None)
            continue
        mask = np.zeros((8, 8), dtype=np.uint8)
        for r in range(8):
            lo = tile[r]
            hi = tile[8 + r]
            for c in range(8):
                mask[r, c] = ((lo >> (7 - c)) & 1) | (((hi >> (7 - c)) & 1) << 1)
        tiles.append(mask)
    return tiles


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("rom")
    ap.add_argument("frame")
    ap.add_argument("--font-base", default="0000")
    ap.add_argument("--bg", default=None, help="backdrop pixel value (default: most common)")
    ap.add_argument("--rows", default="0:30")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    base = int(args.font_base, 16)
    tiles = font_tiles(args.rom, base)
    img = load(args.frame)
    vals, counts = np.unique(img, return_counts=True)
    bg = int(vals[np.argmax(counts)]) if args.bg is None else int(args.bg, 16)

    r0, r1 = (int(x) for x in args.rows.split(":"))
    lines = []
    for row in range(r0, r1):
        line = []
        for col in range(32):
            cell = img[row * 8:(row + 1) * 8, col * 8:(col + 1) * 8]
            on = (cell != bg)
            if not on.any():
                line.append(" ")
                continue
            best, bestscore = "?", -1
            for t, mask in enumerate(tiles):
                if mask is None:
                    continue
                # score = matching bits over the 64 pixels
                score = int((mask == on.astype(np.uint8)).sum())
                if score > bestscore:
                    bestscore, best = score, chr(t) if 32 <= t < 127 else "?"
            line.append(best if bestscore >= 60 else "?")
        lines.append("".join(line).rstrip())
    print("\n".join("%2d| %s" % (r0 + i, l) for i, l in enumerate(lines)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

sys.path.insert(0,'/task/tools')
import numpy as np
sys.argv=['x']
from probe import build, run_both

# Poll the vblank flag (that read may suppress the NMI for this frame), then
# wait K*5 cycles and enable the NMI.  Report whether the NMI fired.
TPL = """
start:  sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        lda #$00
        sta $20
        jsr vwait
        jsr vwait
        jsr vwait
        ldx #%d
dl:     dex
        bne dl
        lda #$80
        sta $2000
        ldy #160
dl2:    dey
        bne dl2
        lda $20
        pha
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
        pla
        sta $2007
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
spin:   jmp spin
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts
nmi:    inc $20
        rti
irq:    rti
"""
def one(k):
    rom = build(TPL % k, vectors=("nmi","start","irq"))
    path = '/task/tmp/supp2_%d.nes' % k
    ref, mine = run_both(path, rom, frames=8)
    return (k, int(ref[-1][0,0]), int(mine[-1][0,0]))
ks = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,14,20,30,50,80,120,160,220,300,400,500,600,700]
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as ex:
    for k,r,m in ex.map(one, ks):
        print("delay %4d cyc (%5d dots) after the read: ref=%d mine=%d %s"
              % (k*5, k*15, r, m, "" if r==m else "<-- DIFF"))

        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        jsr vwait
        jsr vwait
        ; noise: halt=1, constant volume 15
        lda #$30

        lda #$08
        sta $400F
        lda #$08

spin:   jmp spin
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts
nmi:    rti
irq:    rti
"""

def one(args):

    e = (mode<<7) | per

    base='/task/tmp/noise_%d_%d' % (mode, per)

    subprocess.run(['/task/target/release/nesrun',base+'.nes','40','--wav',mine],cwd='/task',capture_output=True,timeout=200)

    except Exception as ex:
        return (mode,per,None,None,str(ex)[:40])
    n=min(len(r),len(m)); s=int(0.3*n)
    a=r[s:n]; b=m[s:n]

    return (mode,per,rms,sig,'')
jobs=[(mo,pe) for mo in (0,1) for pe in range(16)]

        if err: print('mode %d per %2d ERR %s' % (mode,per,err)); continue
        flag = '' if rms < 50 else '  <-- DIFF'
        if rms >= 50: bad.append((mode,per,rms))

        idx=np.where(fs[1:] < pk*0.25)[0]

    print('cfg %s: ref corner=%6.0f Hz mine corner=%6.0f Hz  ratio=%.3f' % (cfg, corner(fa), corner(fb), corner(fb)/max(corner(fa),1)))

}

        ldy #%(outer)d

        pla
        pha
        sta $22
        rti
irq:    inc $21
        pla
        pha
        sta $23

"""

import numpy as np

from asm6502 import Assembler
from mkrom import build_rom

HEAD = """
start:  sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        jsr vwait
        lda #$FF
        sta $02FF
        lda #$C0
        sta $0200
        lda #$C1
        sta $0300
        jmp ($02FF)
"""
def pad_to(a, target):
    while a.pc < target:
        a.line("nop")

a = Assembler(origin=0xC000)
for line in HEAD.splitlines():
    a.line(line)
pad_to(a, 0xC0FF)
# buggy target ($C0FF): paint $0F
for line in "lda #$0F\njmp paint\n".splitlines(): a.line(line)
pad_to(a, 0xC1FF)
# correct target ($C1FF): paint $30
for line in "lda #$30\njmp paint\n".splitlines(): a.line(line)
for line in """

        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
        pla
        sta $2007
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
spin:   jmp spin
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts
nmi:    rti
irq:    rti
""".splitlines(): a.line(line)
code = bytearray(a.assemble())
bank = bytearray(b"\xea" * 0x4000)
bank[0:len(code)] = code
v = [a.labels[x] for x in ("nmi","start","irq")]
for k in range(3):
    bank[0x3FFA + k*2] = v[k] & 0xFF
    bank[0x3FFA + k*2 + 1] = (v[k] >> 8) & 0xFF
rom = build_rom(bytes(bank) * 2, b"", 0, "horizontal", 0, False, 0)
ref, mine = run_both('/task/tmp/ji_probe.nes', rom, frames=4)
r=int(ref[-1][0,0]); m=int(mine[-1][0,0])
print('JMP ($02FF) with low=$FF: ref=%02X mine=%02X %s   (0F = NMOS wrap bug, 30 = reads the right page)' % (r, m, 'OK' if r==m else '<-- DIFF'))
PYEOF

"""Shared helpers: a probe ROM that shows a byte as two hex digits on screen."""
import numpy as np

GLYPHS = {
 0:"0110010101100101011001010110010101100101011001010110011000000000",
}
DIGITS = {
 '0':'01111100'+'11000110'+'11000110'+'11000110'+'11000110'+'11000110'+'01111100'+'00000000',
 '1':'00110000'+'01110000'+'00110000'+'00110000'+'00110000'+'00110000'+'11111100'+'00000000',
 '2':'01111000'+'11001100'+'00001100'+'00011000'+'00110000'+'01100000'+'11111100'+'00000000',
 '3':'01111000'+'11001100'+'00001100'+'00111000'+'00001100'+'11001100'+'01111000'+'00000000',
 '4':'00011000'+'00111000'+'01111000'+'11011000'+'11111110'+'00011000'+'00011000'+'00000000',
 '5':'11111100'+'11000000'+'11111000'+'00001100'+'00001100'+'11001100'+'01111000'+'00000000',
 '6':'00111000'+'01100000'+'11000000'+'11111000'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'01111000'+'00000000',
 '7':'11111100'+'11001100'+'00001100'+'00011000'+'00110000'+'00110000'+'00110000'+'00000000',
 '8':'01111000'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'01111000'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'01111000'+'00000000',
 '9':'01111000'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'01111100'+'00001100'+'00011000'+'01110000'+'00000000',
 'A':'00110000'+'01111000'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'11111100'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'00000000',
 'B':'11111000'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'11111000'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'11111000'+'00000000',
 'C':'01111000'+'11001100'+'11000000'+'11000000'+'11000000'+'11001100'+'01111000'+'00000000',
 'D':'11110000'+'11011000'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'11001100'+'11011000'+'11110000'+'00000000',
 'E':'11111100'+'11000000'+'11000000'+'11111000'+'11000000'+'11000000'+'11111100'+'00000000',
 'F':'11111100'+'11000000'+'11000000'+'11111000'+'11000000'+'11000000'+'11000000'+'00000000',
}
def chr_ram_font():
    """Return an 8 KiB CHR image with ASCII-hex tiles at indices 0..15."""
    chr_ = bytearray(8192)
    for i in range(16):
        pat = DIGITS['0123456789ABCDEF'[i]]
        for row in range(8):
            bits = pat[row*8:(row+1)*8]
            lo = 0
            for c, b in enumerate(bits):
                if b == '1':
                    lo |= 0x80 >> c
            chr_[i*16 + row] = lo
            chr_[i*16 + 8 + row] = lo      # both bitplanes -> colour 3
    return bytes(chr_)

def hextext(chr_path=None):
    """Return a texture dict for readtext: tile index -> character."""
    return {'chr': chr_ram_font() if chr_path is None else None,
            'map': {i: '0123456789ABCDEF'[i] for i in range(16)}}
PY

# decode: the nametable tile at (0,0)-(0,1) renders as hex digits at row 0
def digits(frame):
    # crude OCR: match the 8x8 cells against the font
    font = hexfont.chr_ram_font()
    out = []
    for col in (0, 1):
        cell = frame[0:8, col*8:(col+1)*8]
        best, bestscore = '?', -1
        for t in list(range(0x30, 0x3A)) + list(range(0x41, 0x47)):
            pat = [[(font[t*16+r] >> (7-c)) & 1 for c in range(8)] for r in range(8)]
            score = 0
            for r in range(8):
                for c in range(8):
                    v = 1 if cell[r, c] != 0 else 0
                    if pat[r][c] == v: score += 1
            if score > bestscore: bestscore, best = score, '0123456789ABCDEF'[(t-0x30) if t < 0x3A else (t-0x41+10)]
        out.append(best)
    return ''.join(out)
print('NMI handler X (hex) per frame:')
print('ref ', [digits(f) for f in ref])
print('mine', [digits(f) for f in mine])
PYEOF

    font = hexfont.chr_ram_font()
    out = []
    for col in (0, 1):

        best, bestscore = '?', -1
        for t in list(range(0x30, 0x3A)) + list(range(0x41, 0x47)):
            pat = [[(font[t*16+r] >> (7-c)) & 1 for c in range(8)] for r in range(8)]

            if score > bestscore:

                best = '0123456789ABCDEF'[(t-0x30) if t < 0x3A else (t-0x41+10)]

    S=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(s*np.hanning(len(s))))

EOF

cd /task && cat >> tools/hexfont.py <<'PYEOF'


def decode_screen(frame):
    """Decode a 256x240 index framebuffer rendered with the hex font into a
    list of 960 characters (32 tiles per row, values from chr_ram_font)."""
    font = chr_ram_font()
    # build glyph bitmaps for every tile index
    def bits(t):
        return [[(font[t * 16 + r] >> (7 - c)) & 1 for c in range(8)] for r in range(8)]
    cands = list(range(256))
    out = []
    for ty in range(30):
        for tx in range(32):
            cell = frame[ty * 8:ty * 8 + 8, tx * 8:tx * 8 + 8]
            on = [[1 if cell[r, c] == 0x30 else 0 for c in range(8)] for r in range(8)]
            best, bs = '?', -1
            for t in cands:
                p = bits(t)
                s = sum(1 for r in range(8) for c in range(8) if p[r][c] == on[r][c])
                if s > bs:
                    bs, best = s, t
            out.append(chr(best) if 0x30 <= best <= 0x7A else '.')
    return out
PYEOF

        d_aa=aa-aa.mean(); d_bb=bb-bb.mean()
        den=(np.sqrt((d_aa**2).sum())*np.sqrt((d_bb**2).sum()))
        c=(d_aa*d_bb).sum()/den if den>0 else 0
        r=np.sqrt(((aa-bb)**2).mean())
        if c>best[1]: best=(off,c,r)
    aa=a[s:e]; bb0=b[s:e]; m=min(len(aa),len(bb0))
    d0=aa[:m]-aa[:m].mean(); d1=bb0[:m]-bb0[:m].mean()
    c0=(d0*d1).sum()/(np.sqrt((d0**2).sum())*np.sqrt((d1**2).sum()))
    print('%5d    %+d        %.4f       %.4f     %.1f' % (k, best[0], best[1], c0, best[2]))
EOF

import sys

        sta $2000
        sta $2001

        lda #$3F

        sta $2007

# Session: NMI acceptance model + power-on CPU/PPU alignment

## Fixed: power-on alignment was one PPU dot early
The ABI fixes the power-on state exactly: "at that same moment the PPU is at
scanline 0, dot 25 (the reset sequence has run with the PPU clocking from
scanline 0, dot 0)".  Eight CPU cycles clock 24 dots, so one further PPU dot
is needed.  Measured with a *free-running* raster-band probe (no vblank wait
anywhere: a fixed delay from reset, then a mid-frame palette-hack write whose
band edge is dot-exact): before the fix the band was at dot 104 vs the
reference's 105; after, both are at 105 for the same probe.

NOTE: the earlier `POWER_DOTS` knob was inert -- `ppu_only_dot` called
`process_dot` without `advance()`, so it never moved the dot counter.  That is
why previous phase experiments showed "no effect".

## Verified: NMI acceptance timing model
Built a probe with loops of length 5/7/9/11 cycles whose iteration count at the
NMI is painted through the backdrop-palette hack, so the painted value gives the
acceptance to the cycle (mod 64 * loop length).  Result over 24 frames x 4
lengths:
* immediate pending (no extra delay): **identical to the reference** in all 96
  comparisons;
* pending delayed by 1/2/3 cycles: mine is one loop iteration late on ~1/3 of
  frames for L=5 and on some frames for L=7/9/11.
So the immediate-pending model is the correct one and was kept (default
NMI_DELAY=0; the knob remains for diagnosis).

## Investigated, not explained: robotfindskitten message-box raster offset
With A held from frame 0, rfK draws its message box with a "palette stream"
while rendering is off (the backdrop shows palette[$3F00|v&0x1F] as v walks
through palette RAM).  At frame 12 my bands sit 18-19 dots earlier than the
reference's (identical run lengths, so it is a pure shift).  A one-cycle NMI
delay "fixed" it (7 px vs 79) but the loop probe above proves that model wrong,
i.e. it was masking a different bug; reverted.  The game's intro is
*free-running* (no NMI/$2002 frame sync: $885C's $E0 loop never executes in
this phase), so the offset is a constant ~6 CPU cycles of timeline difference,
not a phase difference (the phase probe matches to the dot).  Candidate causes
ruled out by sweep (no effect on rp_a0): OAM DMA alignment mode (0-3), PPU
warm-up length (29650/29658/29660/29700), first-frame skip, frame extra dots,
palette write delay, NMI sample phase (0/1/2), odd-frame skip dot.

## Remaining differences in the real games
All four games are now pixel-perfect at 1000 frames except a 1-10 pixel
artifact in **row 0 only**, on frames where the palette changes: the frame
boundary ends up to 21 dots after the PPU wrap (instruction granularity), so
the first pixels of scanline 0 are re-rendered before `emu_run_frame` returns,
one dot of the boundary is in the reference's next call.  Removing it needs a
dot-precise frame boundary, i.e. a CPU that can be suspended mid-instruction.
EOF
sleep 100; tail -38 /tmp/suite_final2.txt

def rd(p):

## What the reference's first samples are
Every reference recording starts with the same fixed 100-sample transient

idle level: the NES DACs are unipolar, so the mixer has a constant offset where
mine had none.

## Fix
* `MIX_DC` (apu.rs) is now 0.25 of the mixer's full scale and is added as a
  *constant to the mixer output*.  Previously the knob fed the *zero entries*
  of the pulse/TND tables, which put a huge discontinuity between table entry
  0 and entry 1 and produced audible clicks (file-fixers rms 225 -> 645).

  sample back by about one FIR group delay, and the reference's chain is
  *running* during that window.  Run the chain (HP1, HP2, LP, FIR) that many
  times with the current mixer value before the first output sample, discarding
  the result.  Calibrated: 16 -> 12.6 rms on rfK, 17 -> 2.2, 18 -> 5.0.

Session complete with a **verified audio improvement**.

## What was wrong

Every reference recording begins with the *same* fixed 100-sample transient (identical across all ROMs to the sample: `6295, 7314, 6653, 6284, 5779, 5320 …`). It is the output filter chain's response to the NES mixer's **unipolar DAC idle offset**, plus the fact that the reference's chain is already *running* while my first samples are held back by the start-up delay. My emulator had neither, so it began with silence.

## Changes

**`src/apu.rs`** — `MIX_DC = 0.25` (of mixer full scale) added as a *constant to the mixer output*. The knob previously fed the pulse/TND tables' *zero entries*, which put a huge discontinuity between table entry 0 and entry 1 and produced audible clicks (file-fixers rms 225 → **645** when enabled that way).

**`src/system.rs`** — `AUDIO_PREWARM = 17`: the chain (HP1 → HP2 → LP → FIR) runs 17 times with the current mixer value before the first emitted sample, covering the `AUDIO_START_DELAY` window. Calibrated: 16 → 12.6, 17 → **2.2**, 18 → 5.0 rms on robotfindskitten.

## Measured effect (600 frames, oracle reference)

| ROM | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| robotfindskitten | rms 30.9, corr 0.9993, 99.86% equal | **rms 1.6, corr 0.9993, 99.94% equal** |
| rhde | rms 32.8, 99.73% | **rms 11.0, corr 0.9843, 99.80%** |
| file-fixers | rms 259.2, corr 0.9675 | **rms 257.4, corr 0.9682** |
| stallar | rms 216.3, corr 0.8999 | **rms 214.1, corr 0.9024** |

## Verified unchanged / remaining

- Video: suite total 9703/10500; games at 1000 frames 999 / 999 / 996 / 992 exact, all residuals ≤ 21 px confined to row 0.
- **No drift**: 5000-frame robotfindskitten run = 4999/5000 frames exact, **2 differing pixels total**.
- The remaining audio gap in the music games is *filter ringing at note onsets* (mine: `53, -53, -93, 399, 4388, 6212`; reference: `17, 21, 26, 31, 27, -6, -988`) — the 35-tap anti-alias FIR's step response. Replacing it with minimum-phase IIR low-passes was measured and is far worse (corr **0.036 vs 0.978**), so the FIR stays.
- Also tried and rejected with numbers (all reverted): +1 PPU dot at power-on (suite 9703 → 6697), ending frames before the wrap to kill the row-0 artifact (rfK 599 → 586/600), delaying NMI acceptance (the 5/7/9/11-cycle loop probe proves the immediate model matches the reference 96/96), and lowering the pre-FIR low-pass corner.

`cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean, `tools/abitest.py` → **ABI OK**; all findings recorded in `tools/STATUS.md`.

import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/task/tools')
sys.argv=['sw']
from probe import build, run_both
import numpy as np
# Sync to the NMI, wait a tuned number of cycles so that a single $2002 read
# lands D cycles before the next vblank set, then wait for the next NMI and
# paint.  If the read suppressed the following set, the paint happens one
# frame later.  Comparing the paint frame between the emulators shows whether
# the suppression window matches.
TPL = """
start:  sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        jsr vwait
        jsr vwait
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
        lda #$0F
        sta $2007
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $10
        lda #$80
        sta $2000
        ; wait for the first NMI
w1:     lda $10
        beq w1
        ; long delay: outer loop of %(outer)d * 256 + %(inner)d iterations of 5 cycles
        ldy #$00
outer:  ldx #$00
inner:  dex
        bne inner
        dey
        cpy #%(outer)d
        bne outer
        ; fine tail: %(tail)d extra cycles via nops/bit
        %(taillines)s
        ; the read under test
        bit $2002
        lda $10
        sta $12
w2:     lda $10
        cmp $12
        beq w2
        ; paint white and spin
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
        lda #$30
        sta $2007
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
spin:   jmp spin
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts
nmi:    inc $10
        rti
irq:    rti
"""
def make(outer, inner, tail):
    # tail cycles as nops(2)/bit(3)
    lines=[]
    t=tail
    while t >= 3:
        lines.append("bit $00"); t -= 3
    while t >= 2:
        lines.append("nop"); t -= 2
    return TPL % {'outer': outer, 'inner': inner, 'tail': t, 'taillines': "\n        ".join(lines)}
# 23*256 + 68 = 5956 iterations of 5 cycles = 29780 cycles
for (outer, inner, tail) in ((23,68,0),(23,67,0),(23,69,0),(23,66,0),(23,70,0)):
    text = make(outer, inner, tail)
    rom = build(text, vectors=("nmi","start","irq"))
    path='/task/tmp/suppwin.nes'
    ref, mine = run_both(path, rom, frames=8)
    def flip(frames):
        for f,fr in enumerate(frames):
            if 0x30 in set(fr.flatten().tolist()): return f
        return None
    print('outer=%d inner=%d: ref flip=%s mine flip=%s' % (outer, inner, flip(ref), flip(mine)))

## Root cause of the row-0 artefacts pinned down
Two probes settle it:
* A "visibility phase" probe (the NMI handler alternates the backdrop colour)
  shows both emulators flip at the same frame - vblank writes become visible at
  the same time.
* The single-read probe shows the *difference*: on the frame after the paint,
  the reference's frame already contains 2 pixels of the *new* palette in
  row 0, ours contains 0.  Those pixels are the first pixels of the next
  frame's scanline 0 rendered before `emu_run_frame` returns.
So the reference's frame boundary is *dot/cpu-cycle precise* (it stops a few
dots past the wrap - 2 here) while ours stops at the next *instruction*
boundary, up to 21 dots past.  That granularity difference is exactly what the
games' row-0 artefacts are (ours re-renders up to 7 cycles' worth of scanline 0
with the new palette, the reference 0-2 dots' worth).  Fixing it needs a CPU
that can be suspended mid-instruction.
Also verified this session: `PAL_DELAY` (0..8) does not change this - the
palette write latency is not the mechanism.

## Verified: NMI count parity in vblank-write scenarios
A probe that performs one controlled `bit $2002` at a swept delay and then
paints the NMI counter shows byte-identical counters in both emulators at every
frame, for three delay configurations - so no NMI is lost or gained, and the
earlier "paint frame" mismatches are purely the boundary-granularity effect
above, not a suppression difference.
EOF

    eq=int((aa==bb).sum())

import wave, numpy as np, glob
D=glob.glob('/task/.oracle-out/aw')[-1]
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); return np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float64)
STEP=100.24
def toggle_steps(x, s=3000, n=100):
    k=np.ones(45)/45.0
    sm=np.convolve(x[s:], k, 'same')
    sg=np.sign(sm)
    # ignore small magnitudes (near-zero crossings)
    thr=0.15*np.percentile(np.abs(sm),90)
    tog=[]
    for i in range(1,len(sg)):
        if sg[i]!=sg[i-1] and abs(sm[i])>thr:
            tog.append(i)
    # convert to step indices
    return [int(round(t/STEP)) for t in tog[:n]]
a=toggle_steps(rd(D+'/r.wav'))
b=toggle_steps(rd(D+'/m.wav'))
print('ref  toggle steps:', a[:24])
print('mine toggle steps:', b[:24])
da=np.diff(a); db=np.diff(b)
print('ref  intervals:', da[:20].tolist())
print('mine intervals:', db[:20].tolist())
# search for an interval alignment
best=None
for sh in range(-10,11):
    if sh>=0: aa=da; bb=db[sh:]
    else: aa=da[-sh:]; bb=db
    m=min(len(aa),len(bb))
    if m<10: continue
    sc=int((aa[:m]==bb[:m]).sum())
    if best is None or sc>best[1]: best=(sh,sc,m)
print('best interval match:', best)
EOF

EOF

def lfsr(tap, n=40000, init=1):
    s=init & 0x7FFF
    bits=[]
    for _ in range(n):
        bits.append(s & 1)
        fb = (s & 1) ^ ((s >> tap) & 1)
        s = ((s >> 1) | (fb << 14)) & 0x7FFF
    return bits

    print('tap=%d: ones(bit0)=%d/%d = %.3f  first 30: %s' % (tap, sum(b), len(b), sum(b)/len(b), ''.join(map(str,b[:30]))))
EOF

import numpy as np
SR=44100.0
def hp_coef(hz):
    rc=1.0/(2*np.pi*hz); dt=1.0/SR; return rc/(rc+dt)
def lp_coef(hz):
    rc=1.0/(2*np.pi*hz); dt=1.0/SR; return dt/(rc+dt)
COEFFS=np.array([-0.0000000000,-0.0000582377,0.0000971652,0.0003321966,-0.0013859498,0.0020410250,-0.0002454556,
-0.0049364911,0.0103932113,-0.0088657946,-0.0054848168,0.0282752741,-0.0409680922,0.0191226842,
0.0492957274,-0.1486955687,0.2382745806,0.7256170843,0.2382745806,-0.1486955687,0.0492957274,
0.0191226842,-0.0409680922,0.0282752741,-0.0054848168,-0.0088657946,0.0103932113,-0.0049364911,
-0.0002454556,0.0020410250,-0.0013859498,0.0003321966,0.0000971652,-0.0000582377,-0.0000000000])
print('FIR coeff sum=%.4f, gain at DC=%.4f' % (COEFFS.sum(), COEFFS.sum()))
# frequency response of the HP pair and the FIR at 441 Hz
def hp_resp(hz, f):
    a=hp_coef(hz); z=np.exp(-2j*np.pi*f/SR)
    return a*(1-z)/(1-a*z)
def lp_resp(hz, f):
    a=lp_coef(hz); z=np.exp(-2j*np.pi*f/SR)
    return a/(1-(1-a)*z)
f0=441.0
h=hp_resp(90,f0)*hp_resp(440,f0)*lp_resp(40000,f0)
z=np.exp(-2j*np.pi*f0/SR)
fir=sum(c*z**k for k,c in enumerate(COEFFS))
print('|HP1*HP2*LP| at 441 Hz = %.4f ; |FIR| = %.4f' % (abs(h), abs(fir)))
# time-domain: 50% square through the chain
N=44100
t=np.arange(N)
sq=np.where((np.floor(t*f0/SR*2)%2)==0, 1.0, 0.0)
x=(sq-0.5)*2*0.0744   # AC-coupled square, +-0.0744
a1=hp_coef(90); a2=hp_coef(440); a3=lp_coef(40000)
y1=np.zeros(N); y2=np.zeros(N); y3=np.zeros(N)
x1=0.0; x2=0.0; l=0.0
for i in range(N):
    y1[i]=a1*( (y1[i-1] if i else 0.0) + x[i] - (x[i-1] if i else 0.0) )
    y2[i]=a2*( (y2[i-1] if i else 0.0) + y1[i] - (y1[i-1] if i else 0.0) )
    y3[i]=l + a3*(y2[i]-l); l=y3[i]
fir_out=np.convolve(y3, COEFFS, 'same')
print('rms of x=%.5f  y3=%.5f  fir_out=%.5f  scaled(y3)=%.0f  scaled(fir)=%.0f' % (
    x.std(), y3.std(), fir_out.std(), y3.std()*32000, fir_out.std()*32000))
EOF

import sys, os

from probe import build, run_both
import numpy as np

def asm_for(target):
    # pick (out, inn) with cycles = out*(5*inn+9) - 1 closest to target
    best=None
    for inn in range(1,256):
        per = 5*inn+9
        out = max(1, round((target+1)/per))
        if out>255: continue
        cyc = out*per - 1 + 5   # + lda/sta (5)
        if best is None or abs(cyc-target)<abs(best[0]-target): best=(cyc,out,inn)
    cyc,out,inn = best
    return cyc, out, inn

        bne .d2
        dec $12

""" % (out, inn)
    chr_ = bytearray(8192)

def spec(sig, a, b):
    seg=sig[a:b]
    sp=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(seg*np.hanning(len(seg)))); f=np.fft.rfftfreq(len(seg),1/44100.0)

from probe import build

        lda #$08

        sta $400E
        lda #$FF
        sta $400F
""" % period, vectors=("nmi","start","irq"))
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); return np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float64)
d='/task/.oracle-out/aw/'
PERIOD=0x0D
path='/task/tmp/nz_long.nes'; open(path,'wb').write(mk(PERIOD))
FRAMES=400
subprocess.run(['oracle','run',path,str(FRAMES),'--dump-audio',d+'lr.wav'],cwd='/task',capture_output=True)
subprocess.run(['/task/tools/nesrun_trace',path,str(FRAMES),'--wav',d+'lm.wav'],cwd='/task',capture_output=True)
def decode(x):
    mid=(x.max()+x.min())/2.0
    s=(x>mid).astype(np.int8)
    # sample the level in the middle of each run
    idx=np.nonzero(np.diff(s)!=0)[0]
    starts=np.concatenate(([ -1 ], idx))
    ends=np.concatenate((idx, [len(s)-1]))
    bits=[]
    lens=[]
    for a,b in zip(starts,ends):
        if b-a<2: continue
        m=(a+b)//2
        bits.append(1 if s[m] else 0)
        lens.append(b-a)
    return np.array(bits,dtype=np.int8), np.array(lens)

best=[]

def decode(x, period_cycles, t0):
    T = period_cycles/SR*(SR* (CPU/SR)/SR)  # samples per bit = period_cycles / (CPU/SR)
    T = period_cycles/(CPU/SR)

    lo = np.minimum(idx+1, len(x)-1)

    csum = np.concatenate(([0.0], np.cumsum(x)))
    means = (csum[hi]-csum[lo])/np.maximum(hi-lo,1)

    sep = abs(means[bits==1].mean()-means[bits==0].mean()) if 0<bits.sum()<len(bits) else 0.0

import wave, os, sys, subprocess
import numpy as np
CPU=1789772.7; SR=44100.0
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); return np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float64)
def lp(x, n=25):
    k=np.ones(n)/n
    return np.convolve(x,k,mode='same')
def decode(x, period_cycles, t0):
    T = period_cycles/(CPU/SR)
    n = int((len(x)-t0)/T)
    idx = (t0 + np.arange(n)*T).astype(int)
    lo = np.minimum(idx+1, len(x)-1); hi = np.minimum(idx+int(T)-1, len(x)-1)
    csum = np.concatenate(([0.0], np.cumsum(x)))
    means = (csum[hi]-csum[lo])/np.maximum(hi-lo,1)
    m = np.median(means)
    bits = (means>m).astype(np.int8)
    sep = abs(means[bits==1].mean()-means[bits==0].mean()) if 0<bits.sum()<len(bits) else 0.0
    return bits, sep
def best_phase(x, P):
    best=None
    for t0 in range(0,40):
        bits,sep=decode(x,P,t0)
        if best is None or sep>best[0]: best=(sep,t0)
    return best[1]
def align(bits_a, bits_b, window=300, maxoff=None):
    """find offset o where bits_a[o:o+window] == bits_b[:window]"""
    if maxoff is None: maxoff=len(bits_a)-window
    best=(0,0)
    for off in range(0,maxoff):
        m=float((bits_a[off:off+window]==bits_b[:window]).mean())
        if m>best[0]: best=(m,off)
    return best

import numpy as np
# simulate the NES noise LFSR (mode 0): seed 1, fb = bit0 ^ bit1, shift right, bit14 = fb
def seq(n, tap=1):
    s=1; out=[]
    for i in range(n):
        out.append(1 - (s & 1))      # gate passes volume when bit0 == 0
        fb=((s & 1) ^ ((s >> tap) & 1)) & 1
        s=((s >> 1) | (fb << 14)) & 0x7FFF
    return np.array(out, dtype=np.int8)
S=seq(40000)
np.save('/tmp/lfsr_seq.npy', S)

def sim(n, tap=1):

import sys
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from nz_tools import rd, lp
def run_bounds(x, s0=3000, minrun=6):
    y=x[s0:]
    mid=(y.max()+y.min())/2.0
    sg=(y>mid).astype(np.int8)
    idx=np.nonzero(np.diff(sg)!=0)[0]
    bounds=np.concatenate(([0], idx+1, [len(sg)]))
    keep=[]
    for a,b in zip(bounds[:-1], bounds[1:]):
        if b-a>=minrun: keep.append((a,b))
    # transition times = midpoints between consecutive kept runs (where a gap/glitch was merged, the transition is inside)
    ts=[]
    for (a1,b1),(a2,b2) in zip(keep[:-1],keep[1:]):
        ts.append(((b1+a2)/2.0)+s0)
    return np.array(ts)
d='/task/.oracle-out/aw/'
for tag,fn in (('mine','lm.wav'),('ref','lr.wav')):
    x=lp(rd(d+fn),9)
    ts=run_bounds(x)
    best=None
    for T in np.arange(49.6, 50.6, 0.0002):
        ph=(ts/T)-np.round(ts/T)
        disp=float(np.sqrt((ph**2).mean()))
        if best is None or disp<best[0]: best=(disp,T)
    disp,T=best
    print('%s: transitions=%d best T=%.4f samples = %.2f CPU cycles  rms=%.4f bit (%.2f samples)' %
          (tag,len(ts),T,T*40.517,disp,disp*T))

import sys
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from nz_tools import rd, lp
def sim(n, tap=1):
    s=1; out=np.empty(n, dtype=np.int8)
    for i in range(n):
        out[i]=1-(s&1)
        fb=((s&1)^((s>>tap)&1))&1
        s=((s>>1)|(fb<<14))&0x7FFF
    return out
S=sim(65534)
d='/task/.oracle-out/aw/'
T=2032.09/(1789772.7/44100.0)
def dec(x, s0, t0, n, T=T):
    idx=(s0+t0+np.arange(n)*T).astype(int)
    idx=idx[idx+30<len(x)]
    csum=np.concatenate(([0.0],np.cumsum(x)))
    hi=idx+30
    means=(csum[hi]-csum[idx])/30.0
    return (means>np.median(means)).astype(np.int8)
def phase_from_transitions(x, s0=4000):
    y=x[s0:]; m=(y.max()+y.min())/2.0
    sg=(y>m).astype(np.int8)
    i=np.nonzero(np.diff(sg)!=0)[0]
    b=np.concatenate(([0], i+1, [len(sg)]))
    ts=[]
    for p,q in zip(b[:-1],b[1:]):
        if q-p>=10: ts.append((p+q)/2.0+s0)
    ts=np.array(ts)
    ph=(ts/T)%1.0
    ang=ph*2*np.pi
    mean=np.arctan2(np.sin(ang).mean(), np.cos(ang).mean())/(2*np.pi)
    return (mean%1.0)*T
for tag,fn in (('ref','nr.wav'),('mine','nm.wav')):
    x=lp(rd(d+fn),9)
    ph=phase_from_transitions(x)
    bits=dec(x,4000,int(round(ph)),6000)
    n=min(len(bits),5000)
    best=(10**9,None)
    for off in range(0,32767):
        mism=int((S[off:off+n]!=bits[:n]).sum())
        if mism<best[0]: best=(mism,off)
    print('%s: phase=%.1f n=%d best sim offset=%d mism=%d (%.2f%%)' % (tag,ph,n,best[1],best[0],100.0*best[0]/n))

import sys
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from nz_tools import rd
def two_levels(x, s0=6000):
    y=x[s0:]
    lo,hi=y.min(),y.max()
    # histogram
    h,edges=np.histogram(y, bins=200, range=(lo,hi))
    mid=edges[np.argmax(h[20:180])+20]
    low=y[y<mid]; high=y[y>=mid]
    return float(np.median(low)), float(np.median(high)), len(y)
if __name__=='__main__':
    d='/task/.oracle-out/aw/'
    a=rd(d+sys.argv[1]); b=rd(d+sys.argv[2])
    for tag,x in (('ref',a),('mine',b)):
        l,h,n=two_levels(x)
        print('%s: low=%.0f high=%.0f separation=%.0f (n=%d)' % (tag,l,h,h-l,n))

import os, sys, subprocess, wave
sys.path.insert(0,'/task/tools')
from probe import build
import numpy as np
def mkrom(vol, period=0x0F):
    asm = """
start:  sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        lda #$08
        sta $4015
        lda #$%02X
        sta $400C
        lda #$%02X
        sta $400E
        lda #$FF
        sta $400F
loop:   jmp loop
""" % (0x30 | (vol & 0x0F), period)
    return build(asm, vectors=("start","start","start"))
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); return np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float64)
def levels(x, s0=4000):
    y=x[s0:]
    lo,hi=y.min(),y.max()
    h,edges=np.histogram(y, bins=256, range=(lo-1,hi+1))
    # find the largest peak below 25% and above 75% of the range
    q1=np.percentile(y,15); q3=np.percentile(y,85)
    low=np.median(y[y<=q1]); high=np.median(y[y>=q3])
    return float(low), float(high)
d='/task/.oracle-out/aw/'
print(' vol | ref sep | mine sep | ratio')
for vol in range(0,16):
    path='/task/tmp/mix_%02d.nes'%vol
    open(path,'wb').write(mkrom(vol))

import os, sys, subprocess, wave

from probe import build
import numpy as np
def mkrom(period):
    asm = """
start:  sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        lda #$08
        sta $4015
        lda #$3F
        sta $400C
        lda #$%02X
        sta $400E
        lda #$FF
        sta $400F
loop:   jmp loop
""" % period
    return build(asm, vectors=("start","start","start"))
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); return np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float64)
d='/task/.oracle-out/aw/'
def bands(x, s0=8000, n=32768):
    y=x[s0:s0+n]*np.hanning(n)
    sp=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(y)); f=np.fft.rfftfreq(n,1/44100.0)
    out=[]
    for lo,hi in ((500,2000),(2000,6000),(6000,12000),(12000,20000)):
        out.append(float(np.sqrt((sp[(f>=lo)&(f<hi)]**2).mean())))
    return out
for period in (0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14):
    path='/task/tmp/nzr2_%02d.nes'%period; open(path,'wb').write(mkrom(period))
    subprocess.run(['oracle','run',path,'30','--dump-audio',d+'qr.wav'],cwd='/task',capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(['/task/tools/nesrun_trace',path,'30','--wav',d+'qm.wav'],cwd='/task',capture_output=True)
    ra=bands(rd(d+'qr.wav')); rb=bands(rd(d+'qm.wav'))
    print('p=%2d  ref: %s' % (period, ' '.join('%7.0f'%v for v in ra)))
    print('      mine:%s   ratio %s' % (' '.join('%7.0f'%v for v in rb),
          ' '.join('%.2f'%(b/a if a>1 else 0) for a,b in zip(ra,rb))))

    sg=(y>m).astype(np.int8)
    i=np.nonzero(np.diff(sg)!=0)[0]
    b=np.concatenate(([0], i+1, [len(sg)]))

    ang=ph*2*np.pi
    mean=np.arctan2(np.sin(ang).mean(), np.cos(ang).mean())/(2*np.pi)

        inx

        sta $2003

        sta $2004
        lda #$02

cl:     lda #$FF

sys.path.insert(0,'/task/tools')
from asm6502 import Assembler
import importlib.util
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('mkrom','/task/tools/mkrom.py')
mkrom=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(mkrom)
import numpy as np
CODE = """
start:  sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        lda #$20
        sta $12
w0:     ldx #$00
w1:     dex
        bne w1
        dec $12
        bne w0
        jsr vwait
        ; palette 0: backdrop + colours 1..3
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
        lda #$0F
        sta $2007
        lda #$30
        sta $2007
        lda #$10
        sta $2007
        lda #$20
        sta $2007
        ; nametable $2000-$23FF = tile 0
        lda #$20
        sta $2006
        lda #$00
        sta $2006
        ldx #$04
        ldy #$00
        lda #$00
f1:     sta $2007
        iny
        bne f1
        dex
        bne f1
        lda #$00
        sta $2005
        sta $2005
        lda #%d
        sta $8000          ; CNROM: select CHR bank
        lda #$0A
        sta $2001
loop:   jmp loop
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts
"""
def mk(bank):
    a=Assembler(origin=0xC000)
    for line in (CODE % bank).splitlines(): a.line(line)
    code=a.assemble()
    v=a.labels['start']
    prg=bytearray(b"\xEA"*0x4000)
    prg[:len(code)]=code
    for addr in (0xFFFA,0xFFFC,0xFFFE):
        o=addr-0xC000; prg[o]=v&0xFF; prg[o+1]=(v>>8)&0xFF
    # 4 CHR banks of 8 KiB; tile 0 at offset 0: plane0/plane1 for pattern row 0..7
    val_map=[1,2,3,0]
    chrs=[]
    for b in range(4):
        val=val_map[b]
        lo=0xFF if (val & 1) else 0x00
        hi=0xFF if (val & 2) else 0x00
        c=bytearray(b"\x00"*8192)
        for r in range(8):
            c[r*16+0]=lo; c[r*16+8]=hi
        chrs.append(bytes(c))
    return mkrom.build_rom(bytes(prg), b"".join(chrs), 3, "horizontal", 0, False, 0)
base='/task/.oracle-out/cn'; os.makedirs(base,exist_ok=True); os.chmod(base,0o777)
path='/task/tmp/cn.nes'
for bank in range(4):

    subprocess.run(['/task/tools/nesrun_trace',path,'6','--out',base+'/mine'],cwd='/task',capture_output=True)
    out=[]
    for tag,d in (('ref',base+'/ref'),('mine',base+'/mine')):
        a=np.fromfile(d+'/frame_00005.idx',dtype='<u2').reshape(240,256)
        out.append(int(a[100][100])&0x3F)
    print('chr bank %d: ref=$%02X mine=$%02X %s' % (bank,out[0],out[1],'' if out[0]==out[1] else '<-- DIFF'))
PY

start:  sei

        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        lda #$20
        sta $12
w0:     ldx #$00
w1:     dex
        bne w1
        dec $12
        bne w0

        jsr vwait
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006

        sta $E000

        lda $8000
        sta $2007
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$01
        sta $2006
loop:   jmp loop
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts
"""
def mk(bankval):
    # serial bits of bankval (5 bits, LSB first)
    bits=[(bankval >> i) & 1 for i in range(5)]
    a=Assembler(origin=0xC000)
    src=CODE % (bankval, bits[0])
    # emit the 5 serial writes as immediates
    lines=[]
    for line in src.splitlines():

            lines.append(line)

                lines.append('        lda #$%02X' % b)
                lines.append('        sta $E000')
            lines.append('        jmp serdone')
            lines.append('serdone:')
            continue
        if line.strip().startswith('lda #$%02X' % bits[0]) or line.strip().startswith('sta $E000'):
            continue
        lines.append(line)
    for line in lines: a.line(line)
    code=a.assemble()
    v=a.labels['start']
    # PRG: banks 0..2 hold markers, bank 3 ($C000 fixed) holds the code
    banks=[]
    for k in range(3):
        b=bytearray(b"\xEA"*0x4000); b[0]=0x10+k
        banks.append(bytes(b))
    fixed=bytearray(b"\xEA"*0x4000)
    fixed[:len(code)]=code
    for addr in (0xFFFA,0xFFFC,0xFFFE):
        o=addr-0xC000; fixed[o]=v&0xFF; fixed[o+1]=(v>>8)&0xFF
    prg=b"".join(banks)+bytes(fixed)
    # CHR: 16 KiB of zeros (CHR RAM would also work)
    return mkrom.build_rom(prg, bytes(16384), 1, "horizontal", 0, False, 0)

        out.append(int(a[100][100])&0x3F)
    print('prg bank %d: ref=$%02X mine=$%02X %s' % (bankval,out[0],out[1],'' if out[0]==out[1] else '<-- DIFF'))

import os, sys, subprocess
sys.path.insert(0,'/task/tools')
from asm6502 import Assembler
import importlib.util
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('mkrom','/task/tools/mkrom.py')
mkrom=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(mkrom)
import numpy as np
CODE = """
start:  sei
        cld
        ldx #$FF
        txs
        lda #$00
        sta $2000
        sta $2001
        lda #$20
        sta $12
w0:     ldx #$00
w1:     dex
        bne w1
        dec $12
        bne w0
        jsr vwait
        jsr vwait
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$01
        sta $2006
        lda #$%02X
        sta $8000
        lda #$%02X
        sta $8001
        lda $%04X
        sta $2007
        lda #$3F
        sta $2006
        lda #$01
        sta $2006
loop:   jmp loop
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts
"""
def mk(sel, val, read_addr):
    a=Assembler(origin=0xE000)
    for line in (CODE % (sel, val, read_addr)).splitlines(): a.line(line)
    code=a.assemble()
    v=a.labels['start']
    banks=[]
    for n in range(7):
        b=bytearray(b"\xEA"*0x2000); b[0]=0x10+n
        banks.append(bytes(b))
    fixed=bytearray(b"\xEA"*0x2000)
    fixed[:len(code)]=code
    fixed[0x1000]=0x17
    for addr in (0xFFFA,0xFFFC,0xFFFE):
        o=addr-0xE000; fixed[o]=v&0xFF; fixed[o+1]=(v>>8)&0xFF
    prg=b"".join(banks)+bytes(fixed)
    return mkrom.build_rom(prg, b"", 4, "horizontal", 0, False, 0)
base='/task/.oracle-out/mm3p'; os.makedirs(base,exist_ok=True); os.chmod(base,0o777)
path='/task/tmp/mm3p.nes'
def run(label, sel, val, addr, expect):
    open(path,'wb').write(mk(sel,val,addr))
    subprocess.run(['oracle','run',path,'6','--dump-frames',base+'/ref'],cwd='/task',capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(['/task/tools/nesrun_trace',path,'6','--out',base+'/mine'],cwd='/task',capture_output=True)
    out=[]
    for tag,d in (('ref',base+'/ref'),('mine',base+'/mine')):
        a=np.fromfile(d+'/frame_00005.idx',dtype='<u2').reshape(240,256)
        out.append(int(a[100][100])&0x3F)
    ok = 'OK' if out[0]==out[1] else 'DIFF'
    print('%-34s ref=$%02X mine=$%02X expect=$%02X  %s' % (label,out[0],out[1],expect,ok))
# mode 0 (PRG mode bit clear): R6 -> $8000, R7 -> $A000, $C000.. fixed
for n in (0,1,2,5,7):
    run('mode0 R6=%d read $8000'%n, 6, n, 0x8000, 0x10+n if n<7 else 0x17)
for n in (0,3,6):
    run('mode0 R7=%d read $A000'%n, 7, n, 0xA000, 0x10+n if n<7 else 0x17)
run('mode0 fixed $C000', 6, 0, 0xC000, 0x16)
run('mode0 fixed $F000', 6, 0, 0xF000, 0x17)
# mode 1 (PRG mode bit set): R6 -> $C000, $8000 fixed to second-to-last
for n in (1,4,7):
    run('mode1 R6=%d read $C000'%n, 6|0x40, n, 0xC000, 0x10+n if n<7 else 0x17)
run('mode1 fixed $8000', 6|0x40, 0, 0x8000, 0x16)
PY
timeout 900 python3 /tmp/mmc3prg.py

def mk(sel, val):

        hi=0xFF if (val & 2) else 0x00
        c=bytearray(b"\x00"*1024)
        for r in range(8):
            c[r]=lo; c[8+r]=hi
        chrs.append(bytes(c))
    return mkrom.build_rom(prg, b"".join(chrs), 4, "horizontal", 0, False, 0)

start:  sei

        ldx #$FF
        txs

        sta $2001
        lda #$20

def mk(rate, loop=False, disable_irq=True):

loop:   jmp loop
vwait:  bit $2002
        bpl vwait
        rts

    v=a.labels['start']
    prg=bytearray(b"\xEA"*0x8000)
    prg[:len(code)]=code
    for addr in (0x7FFA,0x7FFC,0x7FFE):

        hi=0xFF if (val & 2) else 0
        base=t*16
        for r in range(8):
            c[base+r]=lo; c[base+8+r]=hi
    hdr_flags6 = (mirror & 1) | (0x08 if four else 0) | ((mapper & 0x0F) << 4)

## What this session established

**The reference band-limits its output stage** — measured fresh: at noise period 0 (223 kHz clock) its in-band power is exactly **half** mine, while at period ≥2 we match within 1–2%. Implemented a **CPU-rate anti-alias filter** (`AA_POLES`/`AA_HZ`) and swept it: it reduces the p=0 error (2.05→1.0) but **always** costs the pulse's 12–20 kHz band (0.99→0.75), because that band contains aliased harmonics in *both* emulators. No single LTI filter matches both → left off by default, finding documented.

**`ATTR_DELAY=1` confirmed correct** (the calibrated setting): with it off, rhde collapses from 399/400 to **23/400** and file-fixers 302→108. Valuable independent confirmation of that knob.

**MMC3 IRQ ruled out** for the file-fixers divergence: file-fixers sets sprites at $1000 (so A12 should rise once per line), but tracing shows the A12 *interleaves* nametable ($2000) and pattern ($1FF7) reads **every 4 dots** — below the 9-dot filter — so the counter clocks ~0 times/frame in **both** emulators (frames match, so the reference behaves the same).

**DMC verified against the docs**: my rate table is exactly the documented NTSC table `[428,380,340,320,286,254,226,214,190,160,142,128,106,84,72,54]`; the output unit matches the documented cycle/silence/shift behaviour; playback correlates 0.92–0.98 with the reference (a residual level/timing difference remains, but playback works).

**Row-0 artifact reproduced precisely**: rhde frame 22, exactly 2 pixels at (0,0)–(1,0) with *different colours* — and with **no writes** (palette or VRAM) anywhere near it, so it is purely a shifter-state difference at the first pixels of the first rendered line. Ruled out: palette delay (2–8), shift-while-disabled, reg delay, open-bus decay.

import os, subprocess, re
ROM='/task/dev-roms/test/cpu_interrupts_v2__3-nmi_and_irq.nes'
def run(env_extra):
    env=dict(os.environ); env.update(env_extra)
    p=subprocess.run(['/task/tools/nesrun_trace',ROM,'200','--prgram'],cwd='/task',capture_output=True,env=env,text=True)

    if not lines: return None,None

    if not fs: return None
    a=np.fromfile(os.path.join(d,fs[-1]),dtype='<u2').reshape(240,256)

print('DONE')

cd /task && cat > tools/mkvbl1.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Single-read vblank probe: burn `burn` CPU cycles after power-on, read $2002
exactly once, then paint palette[0] white if bit 7 was set, black otherwise.
Sweeping `burn` maps the exact CPU cycle at which the vblank flag becomes
visible (and where a read suppresses it) for comparison with the reference.

Usage: mkvbl1.py <burn_cycles> <out.nes>
"""
import struct
import sys

ORIGIN = 0xC000


def build(burn: int, origin=ORIGIN) -> bytes:
    code = bytearray()

    def emit(b):
        code.extend(b)

    def bne(target):
        emit(b"\xd0")
        emit(bytes([(target - (len(code) + 1)) & 0xFF]))

    emit(b"\x78\xd8\xa2\xff\x9a")
    emit(b"\xa9\x00\x8d\x00\x20\x8d\x01\x20")
    # Burn exactly `burn` cycles after the 15 cycles emitted so far is not
    # required; the caller sweeps relative values.
    blocks = burn // 1280
    rest = burn - 1280 * blocks
    k = rest // 5
    tail = rest - 5 * k
    tail_instr = []
    if tail % 2 == 1:
        tail_instr.append(b"\xa5\x10")       # lda $10 : 3 cycles
        tail -= 3
    tail_instr.append(b"\xea" * (tail // 2))
    if blocks > 0:
        if blocks > 255:
            raise SystemExit("burn too large")
        emit(b"\xa9" + bytes([blocks]))
        emit(b"\x85\x12")
        outer = len(code)
        emit(b"\xa2\x00")
        inner = len(code)
        emit(b"\xca"); bne(inner)
        emit(b"\xc6\x12")
        bne(outer)
    if k > 0:
        emit(b"\xa2" + bytes([k & 0xFF]))
        top = len(code)
        emit(b"\xca"); bne(top)
    for ins in tail_instr:
        emit(ins)
    emit(b"\xad\x02\x20")                    # lda $2002 (single read)
    emit(b"\x29\x80")                        # and #$80
    emit(b"\xf0\x04")                        # beq +4 -> black
    emit(b"\xa9\x30")                        # white
    emit(b"\xd0\x02")                        # bne +2
    emit(b"\xa9\x0f")                        # black
    emit(b"\x8d\x07\x20")                    # (pal set to $3F00 by then?)
    # point v at palette[0] first
    emit(b"\xa9\x3f\x8d\x06\x20\xa9\x00\x8d\x06\x20")
    # (the sta $2007 above was written before the address set; do it properly)
    spin = len(code)
    emit(b"\x4c" + struct.pack("<H", origin + spin))
    prg = bytearray(0x8000)
    off = origin - 0x8000
    assert off + len(code) <= 0x8000
    prg[off:off + len(code)] = code
    for a in (0x7FFA, 0x7FFC, 0x7FFE):
        prg[a:a + 2] = struct.pack("<H", origin)
    return b"NES\x1a" + bytes([2, 0, 0, 0]) + b"\x00" * 8 + bytes(prg)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    burn = int(sys.argv[1])
    out = sys.argv[2]
    open(out, "wb").write(build(burn))
    print("wrote", out, "burn", burn)

cd /task && cat > tools/mkpatprobe.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pattern-table probe: fills CHR RAM with distinct tiles in tables $0000 and
$1000, sets $2000 = $08 (docs: BG table $1000, sprites $0000), fills the
nametable with tile 1, and displays.  The screen colour reveals which table the
background actually fetches from.

Usage: mkpatprobe.py <out.nes>
"""
import struct
import sys

ORIGIN = 0xE000


class Asm:
    def __init__(self):
        self.code = bytearray()
        self.labels = {}
        self.fixups = []

    def emit(self, b):
        self.code.extend(b)

    def label(self, name):
        self.labels[name] = len(self.code)

    def branch(self, op, target):
        self.emit(bytes([op]))
        self.fixups.append((len(self.code), target))
        self.emit(b"\x00")

    def resolve(self):
        for pos, target in self.fixups:
            off = (self.labels[target] - (pos + 1)) & 0xFF
            self.code[pos] = off


def build() -> bytes:
    a = Asm()
    e, br = a.emit, a.branch
    e(b"\x78\xd8\xa2\xff\x9a")                    # sei cld ldx #$FF txs
    e(b"\xa9\x00\x8d\x00\x20\x8d\x01\x20")        # $2000 = $2001 = 0
    a.label("w1"); e(b"\x2c\x02\x20"); br(0x10, "w1")   # bit $2002 ; bpl w1
    a.label("w2"); e(b"\x2c\x02\x20"); br(0x30, "w2")   # bit $2002 ; bmi w2
    # CHR table $0000: 16 zeros, then tile 1 = 8 x $FF, 8 x $00
    e(b"\xa9\x00\x8d\x06\x20\x8d\x06\x20")
    e(b"\xa2\x10\xa9\x00")
    a.label("c1"); e(b"\x8d\x07\x20\xca"); br(0xD0, "c1")
    e(b"\xa2\x08\xa9\xff")
    a.label("c2"); e(b"\x8d\x07\x20\xca"); br(0xD0, "c2")
    e(b"\xa2\x08\xa9\x00")
    a.label("c3"); e(b"\x8d\x07\x20\xca"); br(0xD0, "c3")
    # CHR table $1000: tile 1 = 8 x $00, 8 x $FF
    e(b"\xa9\x10\x8d\x06\x20\xa9\x10\x8d\x06\x20")
    e(b"\xa2\x08\xa9\x00")
    a.label("c4"); e(b"\x8d\x07\x20\xca"); br(0xD0, "c4")
    e(b"\xa2\x08\xa9\xff")
    a.label("c5"); e(b"\x8d\x07\x20\xca"); br(0xD0, "c5")
    # palette $3F00 = 0F 30 16
    e(b"\xa9\x3f\x8d\x06\x20\xa9\x00\x8d\x06\x20")
    e(b"\xa9\x0f\x8d\x07\x20\xa9\x30\x8d\x07\x20\xa9\x16\x8d\x07\x20")
    # nametable $2000: 960 x tile 1 then 64 x 0
    e(b"\xa9\x20\x8d\x06\x20\xa9\x00\x8d\x06\x20")
    e(b"\xa0\x03")                                # y = 3
    a.label("page"); e(b"\xa2\x00\xa9\x01")
    a.label("pg"); e(b"\x8d\x07\x20\xe8"); br(0xD0, "pg")
    e(b"\x88"); br(0xD0, "page")
    e(b"\xa2\xc0\xa9\x01")                        # 192 more
    a.label("pg2"); e(b"\x8d\x07\x20\xca"); br(0xD0, "pg2")
    e(b"\xa2\x40\xa9\x00")                        # 64 zeros (attribute)
    a.label("pg3"); e(b"\x8d\x07\x20\xca"); br(0xD0, "pg3")
    # scroll 0, $2000 = $08, $2001 = $0A
    e(b"\xa9\x00\x8d\x05\x20\xa9\x00\x8d\x05\x20")
    e(b"\xa9\x08\x8d\x00\x20\xa9\x0a\x8d\x01\x20")
    a.label("spin"); e(b"\x4c" + struct.pack("<H", ORIGIN + len(a.code)))
    a.resolve()
    prg = bytearray(0x4000)
    assert len(a.code) < 0x2000, len(a.code)
    prg[0x2000:0x2000 + len(a.code)] = a.code
    for v in (0x3FFA, 0x3FFC, 0x3FFE):
        prg[v:v + 2] = struct.pack("<H", ORIGIN)
    return b"NES\x1a" + bytes([1, 0, 0, 0]) + b"\x00" * 8 + bytes(prg)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    open(sys.argv[1], "wb").write(build())
    print("wrote", sys.argv[1])

cd /task && cat > tools/mkapuprobe.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""APU mixer probe: sweeps the DMC DAC ($4011 = 0..127, 3 frames each) with all
channels disabled, so the output level directly encodes the mixer's response to
a known digital level.  Comparing the reference's WAV with ours reveals any
mixer curve difference.

Usage: mkapuprobe.py <out.nes>
"""
import struct
import sys

ORIGIN = 0xE000


class Asm:
    def __init__(self):
        self.code = bytearray()
        self.labels = {}
        self.fixups = []

    def emit(self, b):
        self.code.extend(b)

    def label(self, name):
        self.labels[name] = len(self.code)

    def branch(self, op, target):
        self.emit(bytes([op]))
        self.fixups.append((len(self.code), target))
        self.emit(b"\x00")

    def resolve(self):
        for pos, target in self.fixups:
            self.code[pos] = (self.labels[target] - (pos + 1)) & 0xFF


def build() -> bytes:
    a = Asm()
    e, br = a.emit, a.branch
    e(b"\x78\xd8\xa2\xff\x9a")              # sei cld ldx #$FF txs
    e(b"\xa9\x00\x8d\x15\x40")              # $4015 = 0 (all channels off)
    e(b"\xa9\x00\x8d\x11\x40")              # $4011 = 0
    e(b"\xa2\x00")                          # X = level
    a.label("outer")
    # wait ~3 frames using the vblank flag
    for i in range(3):
        a.label("w1%d" % i); e(b"\x2c\x02\x20"); br(0x10, "w1%d" % i)
        a.label("w2%d" % i); e(b"\x2c\x02\x20"); br(0x30, "w2%d" % i)
    e(b"\x8e\x11\x40")                      # sta $4011 (X)
    e(b"\xe8")                              # inx
    e(b"\xe0\x80")                          # cpx #$80
    br(0xD0, "outer")
    a.label("spin"); e(b"\x4c" + struct.pack("<H", ORIGIN + len(a.code)))
    a.resolve()
    prg = bytearray(0x4000)
    prg[0x2000:0x2000 + len(a.code)] = a.code
    for v in (0x3FFA, 0x3FFC, 0x3FFE):
        prg[v:v + 2] = struct.pack("<H", ORIGIN)
    return b"NES\x1a" + bytes([1, 0, 0, 0]) + b"\x00" * 8 + bytes(prg)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    open(sys.argv[1], "wb").write(build())
    print("wrote", sys.argv[1])
PY

cd /task && cat > tools/mkchprobe.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-channel APU probe.  Sets up a single channel at a fixed pitch/volume and
spins, so the reference's WAV can be compared against ours for that channel
alone.

Usage: mkchprobe.py <mode> <out.nes>
Modes: tri, pulse1, pulse2, noise, dmc
"""
import struct
import sys

ORIGIN = 0xE000


class Asm:
    def __init__(self):
        self.code = bytearray()
        self.labels = {}
        self.fixups = []

    def emit(self, b):
        self.code.extend(b)

    def label(self, name):
        self.labels[name] = len(self.code)

    def branch(self, op, target):
        self.emit(bytes([op]))
        self.fixups.append((len(self.code), target))
        self.emit(b"\x00")

    def resolve(self):
        for pos, target in self.fixups:
            self.code[pos] = (self.labels[target] - (pos + 1)) & 0xFF


def build(mode: str) -> bytes:
    a = Asm()
    e, br = a.emit, a.branch
    e(b"\x78\xd8\xa2\xff\x9a")              # sei cld ldx #$FF txs
    e(b"\xa9\x00\x8d\x15\x40")              # $4015 = 0
    e(b"\xa9\x40\x8d\x17\x40")              # $4017 = $40 (frame counter: 4-step, IRQ off)
    if mode == "tri":
        # length halt + linear reload 127; period 558 -> ~100 Hz
        e(b"\xa9\xff\x8d\x08\x40")
        e(b"\xa9\x2e\x8d\x0a\x40")
        e(b"\xa9\x02\x8d\x0b\x40")
        e(b"\xa9\x04\x8d\x15\x40")          # enable triangle
    elif mode in ("pulse1", "pulse2"):
        base = 0x4000 if mode == "pulse1" else 0x4004
        en = 0x01 if mode == "pulse1" else 0x02
        e(b"\xa9\xbf\x8d" + bytes([base & 0xFF, base >> 8]))       # duty 2, halt, const vol 15
        e(b"\xa9\x08\x8d" + bytes([(base + 1) & 0xFF, base >> 8])) # sweep off
        e(b"\xa9\xf8\x8d" + bytes([(base + 2) & 0xFF, base >> 8])) # period low (1016 -> ~110 Hz)
        e(b"\xa9\x03\x8d" + bytes([(base + 3) & 0xFF, base >> 8]))
        e(b"\xa9" + bytes([en]) + b"\x8d\x15\x40")
    elif mode == "noise":
        e(b"\xa9\x3f\x8d\x0c\x40")          # halt, const vol 15
        e(b"\xa9\x04\x8d\x0e\x40")          # mode 0, period index 4
        e(b"\xa9\x08\x8d\x0f\x40")
        e(b"\xa9\x08\x8d\x15\x40")
    elif mode == "dmc":
        e(b"\xa9\x0f\x8d\x10\x40")          # DMC rate index 15, no IRQ, no loop
        e(b"\xa9\x40\x8d\x11\x40")          # direct load $40
        e(b"\xa9\x10\x8d\x15\x40")
    else:
        raise SystemExit("bad mode")
    a.label("spin"); e(b"\x4c" + struct.pack("<H", ORIGIN + len(a.code)))
    a.resolve()
    prg = bytearray(0x4000)
    prg[0x2000:0x2000 + len(a.code)] = a.code
    for v in (0x3FFA, 0x3FFC, 0x3FFE):
        prg[v:v + 2] = struct.pack("<H", ORIGIN)
    return b"NES\x1a" + bytes([1, 0, 0, 0]) + b"\x00" * 8 + bytes(prg)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mode, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    open(out, "wb").write(build(mode))
    print("wrote", out, "mode", mode)
PY

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Empirical tuner for the audio output stage: runs our emulator on probe ROMs
with given knob settings and scores the RMS error against cached reference WAVs."""
import os, subprocess, sys, wave
import numpy as np

ROM = '/task/target/release/nesrun'
PROBES = [('ch_pulse1', 200), ('ch_tri', 200)]
REF = {}

def rd(p):
    w = wave.open(p); n = w.getnframes()
    a = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(n), dtype='<i2').astype(np.float64); w.close()
    return a

def load_refs():
    for name, frames in PROBES:
        REF[name] = rd('/task/.oracle-out/%s/ref.wav' % name)

def run_probe(name, frames, extra_env):
    out = '/tmp/tune_%s.wav' % name
    env = dict(os.environ); env.update(extra_env)
    subprocess.run([ROM, '/task/tmp/%s.nes' % name, str(frames), '--wav', out],
                   capture_output=True, env=env, cwd='/task')
    if not os.path.exists(out): return None
    return rd(out)

def score(extra_env, verbose=False):
    tot = 0.0; parts = []
    for name, frames in PROBES:
        b = run_probe(name, frames, extra_env)
        if b is None: return 1e18, []
        a = REF[name]
        n = min(len(a), len(b))
        e = np.sqrt(((a[:n] - b[:n]) ** 2).mean())
        parts.append((name, e)); tot += e
    if verbose: print('   ', ['%s=%.1f' % p for p in parts])
    return tot / len(PROBES), parts

if __name__ == '__main__':
    load_refs()
    base = {}
    for kv in sys.argv[1:]:
        k, v = kv.split('=')
        base[k] = v
    s, parts = score(base, verbose=True)
    print('score %.3f' % s)
PY
python3 tools/audiotune.py A_HP1=90 A_HP2=440 A_SCALE=32000 2>&1 | tail -3
```

cd /task && cat > tools/mkpulsesweep.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pulse mixer-curve probe: holds pulse 1 at a fixed ~110 Hz duty-2 square wave
while stepping its constant volume 0..15 (3 frames each, twice).  The observed
plateau amplitudes give the mixer's response to each pulse DAC level.

Usage: mkpulsesweep.py <out.nes>
"""
import struct, sys

ORIGIN = 0xE000


class Asm:
    def __init__(self):
        self.code = bytearray(); self.labels = {}; self.fixups = []
    def emit(self, b): self.code.extend(b)
    def label(self, n): self.labels[n] = len(self.code)
    def branch(self, op, t):
        self.emit(bytes([op])); self.fixups.append((len(self.code), t)); self.emit(b"\x00")
    def resolve(self):
        for pos, t in self.fixups:
            self.code[pos] = (self.labels[t] - (pos + 1)) & 0xFF


def build() -> bytes:
    a = Asm(); e, br = a.emit, a.branch
    e(b"\x78\xd8\xa2\xff\x9a")
    e(b"\xa9\x00\x8d\x15\x40")
    e(b"\xa9\x40\x8d\x17\x40")
    e(b"\xa9\x01\x8d\x15\x40")          # enable pulse 1 first (length loads)
    e(b"\xa9\xbf\x8d\x00\x40")          # duty 2, halt, const volume 15
    e(b"\xa9\x08\x8d\x01\x40")          # sweep off
    e(b"\xa9\xf8\x8d\x02\x40")          # period low
    e(b"\xa9\x03\x8d\x03\x40")          # period high
    e(b"\xa2\x00")                      # X = volume
    a.label("outer")
    for i in range(2):
        a.label("w1%d" % i); e(b"\x2c\x02\x20"); br(0x10, "w1%d" % i)
        a.label("w2%d" % i); e(b"\x2c\x02\x20"); br(0x30, "w2%d" % i)
    e(b"\x8a")                          # txa
    e(b"\x09\xb0")                      # ora #$B0  (duty 2, halt, const vol)
    e(b"\x8d\x00\x40")                  # sta $4000
    e(b"\xe8")                          # inx
    e(b"\xe0\x10")                      # cpx #$10
    br(0xD0, "outer")
    e(b"\xa2\x00")                      # second pass
    a.label("outer2")
    for i in range(2):
        a.label("v1%d" % i); e(b"\x2c\x02\x20"); br(0x10, "v1%d" % i)
        a.label("v2%d" % i); e(b"\x2c\x02\x20"); br(0x30, "v2%d" % i)
    e(b"\x8a"); e(b"\x09\xb0"); e(b"\x8d\x00\x40")
    e(b"\xe8"); e(b"\xe0\x10")
    br(0xD0, "outer2")
    a.label("spin"); e(b"\x4c" + struct.pack("<H", ORIGIN + len(a.code)))
    a.resolve()
    prg = bytearray(0x4000)
    prg[0x2000:0x2000 + len(a.code)] = a.code
    for v in (0x3FFA, 0x3FFC, 0x3FFE):
        prg[v:v + 2] = struct.pack("<H", ORIGIN)
    return b"NES\x1a" + bytes([1, 0, 0, 0]) + b"\x00" * 8 + bytes(prg)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    open(sys.argv[1], "wb").write(build())
    print("wrote", sys.argv[1])
PY

import wave, numpy as np
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); n=w.getnframes(); a=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(n),dtype='<i2').astype(np.float64); w.close(); return a
for name,pa,pb in (('ch_tri','.oracle-out/ch_tri/ref.wav','.oracle-out/ch_tri/mine.wav'),

    A=rd(pa); B=rd(pb); n=min(len(A),len(B)); A=A[:n]; B=B[:n]
    N=8192
    # average PSD over windows
    def psd(x):
        acc=np.zeros(N//2+1)
        cnt=0
        for s in range(0,len(x)-N,N//2):
            w=np.hanning(N)
            f=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(x[s:s+N]*w))**2
            acc+=f; cnt+=1

    Pa=psd(A); Pb=psd(B)
    f=np.fft.rfftfreq(N,1/44100)

        print('  %5d-%5d Hz: ref %9.2f mine %9.2f  ratio %.4f' % (lo,hi,ra,rb,ra/rb if rb>0 else 0))

    idx=np.arange(L-1,n)
    X=np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(m, L)[:-1]  # X[i] = m[i..i+L-1]
